clue.text: Crushed fare given to each tender convert

parts.note: a dish is a serving of food, the fare on the table

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters of tender are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is downcast because the food they got didn't suit their soft new beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' looks like a noun for a new believer, but it is the signal to rearrange the six letters of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling crushed and feeling disheartened are both states of being deeply discouraged, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Model scene puts new radio at half-mast

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters of radio are put into a fresh order
half-mast asks for half of the word mast, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A miniature tableau shows a wireless set beside a flag flown at half-mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RADIO into DIORA; 'half' takes MA from MAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model of a scene, often in a museum display.

clue.text: Reserve joins team in decline

parts.note: a sub, or substitute, is a reserve player
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A substitute player joins a team that is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside is to sink or settle lower, to be in decline; the definition works as a verb phrase.

clue.text: Caught in the doorway with fit, so must be nervous

indicators.note: Caught sits inside the doorway, so the letter goes within that word

parts.note: an exit is a way out, a doorway
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a doorway while having a fit is bound to be on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An excitable person is easily agitated, much like someone nervous and highly strung.

clue.text: Dressed or turned over on the bed

indicators.note: turning over the little word or flips it so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you got dressed or just rolled over in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Robed means clothed in a robe, hence dressed.

clue.text: Don't start to listen to an evangelist or reserve

indicators.note: telling the word not to start removes its opening letter

parts.note: to hear is to listen
Mark is one of the four evangelists, writers of the Gospels

explanation.surface: Advice not to begin listening to a preacher, or else to hold back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes the H from HEAR, leaving EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to set them aside, to reserve them for a purpose.

clue.text: This increase could be general

indicators.note: says the letters of general could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A remark that a general might be promoted to a greater rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make bigger, a synonym of increase used as a verb.

clue.text: Awesome acceptance comes after life

indicators.note: the acceptance word is placed after the life word in the answer

parts.note: breath stands for life, as in the breath of life
taking means accepting, as in taking an offer

explanation.surface: Something wonderful follows when a person finally embraces life.
explanation.definitionFit: Something breathtaking is so impressive that it inspires awe, the sense of awesome.

clue.text: Order I must get: right-hand comb with lozenge shape

indicators.note: putting the pieces in order means rearranging them into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
H is an abbreviation for hand, as on a clock or in sailing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to fetch a right-handed comb shaped like a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges I, RH and COMB together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is the diamond or lozenge figure, so rhombic describes something of that shape.

clue.text: Seized food back, having got shown the way

indicators.note: back says the food word is read in reverse

parts.note: grub is slang for food
led means guided, shown the way

explanation.surface: Someone grabs back their food after being guided to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgled means robbed, so goods seized by a thief have been burgled.

clue.text: Eddie's tomcat might well be!

indicators.note: suggests the letters of the phrase could be recast into another form

parts.note: the possessive here supplies its S as a letter

explanation.surface: Observing that a man's pet cat is probably house-trained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might well be' rearranges all twelve letters of EDDIES TOMCAT; the whole clue also describes a pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet tomcat is tamed and house-trained, which is what domesticated means.

clue.text: Linguist sat with a rib broken

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters are smashed apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone who studies languages sat there nursing a broken rib.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabist is a scholar of the Arabic language and culture, so a kind of linguist.

clue.text: Plan — I'd better turn on one gaining weight

indicators.note: says the short form I'd should turn round and read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
A means one, as in a single item
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone advises that a person putting on weight should change direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawing that sets out a design, just as a plan does.

clue.text: To retch, which is endless bliss!

indicators.note: endless means the bliss word loses its final letter

parts.note: heaven is a state of bliss

explanation.surface: A joke that being sick is perfect happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to make the effort of vomiting, the same as to retch.

clue.text: Gloomy members, who do not strike

parts.note: black means dark and gloomy
legs are limbs, which are members of the body

explanation.surface: Miserable people who refuse to join the walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a blackleg is a strike-breaker, someone who works on while colleagues strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Blacklegs are workers who keep working during a strike, so they do not strike.

clue.text: It's receptive, making babe snort

indicators.note: making out of the letters means building a new word from them

explanation.surface: A baby snorting turns out to be very open to impressions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbent soaks things up readily, so it is receptive.

clue.text: Yes-men with absurd cares about a line

indicators.note: the scrambled cares goes about, around, the line word
absurd means nonsensical, so the letters of cares are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: Sycophants with ridiculous worries about a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' asks for the jumbled cares to be split so the line sits in its middle; Yes-men who accord are agreers.
explanation.definitionFit: Accorders are those who agree, so people who always say yes.

clue.text: Tough coal, almost plentiful relative to heat

indicators.note: tough here suggests rough handling, so the letters of coal are knocked about
almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: rich means plentiful or abundant

explanation.surface: Hard coal, nearly abundant, measured by the heat it gives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' rearranges COAL into CALO; 'almost' drops the H of RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Caloric means relating to heat or calories, the definition's sense.

clue.text: Still it's lean and all but stuffed

parts.note: to rest on something is to lean on it

indicators.note: all but means nearly all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: full means stuffed after a big meal

explanation.surface: A diet remark that something is lean yet nearly stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' drops the final L of FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful means quiet and peaceful, as calm as something still.

clue.text: Typical omelette-filler gives pleasure to US soldier

definitions.note: singular in the clue, but the answer is the plural group that mushrooms belong to

parts.note: fun means pleasure or enjoyment
GI is the American term for a soldier

explanation.surface: A mushroom omelette delights an American serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are fungi and a classic omelette filling, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Guesses shapes

definitions.meaning: outlines or forms, as of human bodies

explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to reckon or guess, and figures are also bodily forms or shapes.

clue.text: Some drink G and T like this, it's observed

definitions.text: Some drink G and T like this
definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: some people take their gin and tonic without ice

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means without ice; as one word it is a synonym for spotted or seen.

clue.text: Maltreated and sick, then employed

parts.note: ill means sick
used means employed, put to use

explanation.surface: Someone badly treated, fell ill, and was then exploited at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-used means treated badly or unfairly, which is maltreated.

clue.text: I'm about to be kept by mother — that's an ambition

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the about word goes into the mother word

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A child dependent on their mother says that this is their life goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a cherished hope or goal, an ambition.

clue.text: A target replaced for rowing races

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in different places

explanation.surface: A substitute target is set up for a boat race.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, typically for rowing or sailing.

clue.text: Throw back the clothes, half-affected with my long neck?

indicators.note: throw back means the clothes word is turned round

parts.note: a rig, or rig-out, is an outfit of clothes

indicators.note: half of affected means its first four letters

explanation.surface: Someone throws off the bedclothes, half-pretending to be a long-necked creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw back' reverses RIG to GIR; 'half' takes AFFE from AFFECTED. The answer speaks as 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is the animal famous for its very long neck, so the riddle names it.

clue.text: A pain? Have some tea, Rachel

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An offer of a cuppa to a friend called Rachel who is feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: An earache is a specific pain felt in the ear, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Accustomed to upset mice with acid and salt

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A lab report on getting mice used to acid and salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MICE, ACID and SALT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being acclimatised means having adapted to conditions, being accustomed to them.
